solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, linked answer split by the grid); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Garden hut he sold to eccentric

indicators.note: eccentric means odd or off-centre, so the letters of the words before it are set in a strange new order

explanation.surface: A garden hut has been sold by its owner to an oddball neighbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eccentric' looks like a noun for the buyer, but it is the signal to rearrange HESOLDTO.
explanation.definitionFit: A shed for keeping spades and mowers is a typical small hut at the bottom of a garden.

clue.text: Being broadcast from Barcelona, I reported

indicators.note: from tells us the letters are drawn out of the run of words that follows, crossing the word breaks

explanation.surface: A radio correspondent says she is live on air from Barcelona.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across the end of 'Barcelona', the whole of 'I' and the start of 'reported'.
explanation.definitionFit: A programme that is going out live to listeners right now is said to be transmitting in that phrase.

clue.text: Plant, most unrestrained, abounding

parts.note: the loosest is the most free or unrestrained
rife means abounding or widespread

explanation.surface: A plant spreading wildly, growing everywhere without check.
explanation.definitionFit: Purple and yellow forms of this flowering perennial grow on riverbanks; it is a plant name, not a quarrel.

clue.text: Hackney stained? That's another thing altogether

parts.note: a hackney is a breed of horse used for driving, also a horse for hire
something stained has been made another hue, so it is now of a different colour

explanation.surface: A question about a London borough being stained, answered with a shrug that it is something else entirely.
explanation.walkthrough: Hackney is a London borough, which is what the capital H suggests; here it is the breed of horse.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom is used of a matter quite unlike the one under discussion, a separate thing altogether.

clue.text: See 4
A crown originally, plus tax, for an item of menswear

indicators.note: originally says the crown comes first, ahead of the letter A it follows in the clue

parts.note: CR is the abbreviation for crown, as in the old coin
VAT is value added tax

explanation.surface: Taxing a crown to pay for a man's neckwear, as if it were a shopping receipt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'originally' is an order signal: CR is placed before A, not after it as the clue's wording runs.
explanation.definitionFit: A neckerchief or wide scarf worn by men tucked into an open collar is a classic item of male clothing.

clue.text: Clipper ship?

definitions.meaning: a person or tool that clips or trims is one that cuts
a small fast sailing vessel with one mast, or a ship's boat, is this kind of craft

explanation.surface: A clipper, the fast sailing ship, is asked about.
explanation.walkthrough: A clipper is famously a ship, so the clue seems one idea; split it and 'Clipper' is one who clips.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: one who trims hair or cloth, and a single-masted sailing boat or naval launch.

clue.text: A quiet wood

parts.note: sh is the call for quiet

explanation.surface: A peaceful stretch of woodland.
explanation.definitionFit: The timber of this tree is used for tool handles and cricket stumps, so the tree's name names a wood.

clue.text: A manipulated Dane accommodating a US male, to a sickening degree

indicators.note: accommodating means giving room to, so the second a and US go inside the shuffled letters
manipulated means handled and moved about, so the letters of Dane are worked into a new order

parts.note: US is the United States

explanation.surface: A Dane being manipulated while hosting an American man, until it all becomes sickening.
explanation.walkthrough: The two a's do different jobs: the capital one leads the answer, the small one joins US inside DNEA, which 'manipulated' makes of the Dane, while 'accommodating' signals the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase means until one feels nausea, used of something repeated to the point of disgust.

clue.text: Good turn from Labour's leader, out of character

indicators.note: out of says a letter is taken away, here from the word for character

parts.note: flavour means distinctive character, as in the flavour of a place

indicators.note: leader means the first letter of the word Labour

explanation.surface: A political favour from the Labour leader, done out of character.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of character' reads as a phrase about behaviour; it is split, 'out of' being the removal and 'character' the word losing L.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing someone a kindness or service is a synonym phrase for a helpful act done for another.

clue.text: Going to get fine engraving

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencil leads
an etching is a print made from an engraved plate

explanation.surface: Someone off to collect a fine engraving from a dealer.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer more often means attractive; here it is used literally, going off to bring something back.
explanation.definitionFit: To fetch is to go and bring back, so the participle describes someone on their way to collect something.

clue.text: Short set of instructions needed to make cheese

indicators.note: short means cut down, so the last letter of the word for instructions is dropped

parts.note: a brief is a set of instructions, as given to a barrister

explanation.surface: A recipe card: just a few instructions needed to make cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: A soft French cow's milk variety with a white rind is a famous example of the dairy product.

clue.text: Test team's bonus?

parts.note: a cricket or football team is an eleven
a plus is an advantage or bonus

explanation.surface: A question about whether a sports team is getting a bonus.
explanation.walkthrough: The ELEVEN-PLUS is the exam British children once took at about eleven to decide whether they went to a grammar school.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the name of a British school selection exam, so it is an example of a test.

clue.text: Stand firm

definitions.meaning: in cricket a stand is the runs two batsmen put on together, also called this
a firm owned by partners, as of lawyers or accountants, is this kind of business

explanation.walkthrough: 'Stand firm' reads as an order not to give way; split, it is a cricket term and a business.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: in cricket a pair batting together making runs, and a business owned jointly by partners.

clue.text: Religious hypocrite in sharp sleeveless coat?

parts.note: tart means sharp in taste

indicators.note: sleeveless means losing its outer parts, so the word for coat loses its first and last letters

parts.note: a puffer is a padded quilted jacket or coat

explanation.surface: A sanctimonious churchgoer seen in a smart coat with no sleeves.
explanation.walkthrough: TARTUFFE is the hypocrite of Moliere's comedy, whose name now means one. 'sleeveless' strips PUFFER to UFFE.
explanation.definitionFit: Moliere's title character feigns piety, and his name became a byword for a sanctimonious pretender.

clue.text: Anton, a guy in trouble columnist exposed

indicators.note: in trouble means in a mess, so the letters of the name and a guy are muddled

explanation.surface: A man called Anton, in difficulties, is exposed by a newspaper columnist.
explanation.walkthrough: An AGONY AUNT is a newspaper columnist who answers readers' personal problems.
explanation.definitionFit: Such a writer runs the problem page of a paper or magazine, giving advice, so is a kind of columnist.

clue.text: Part of film is not fictitious, according to report

indicators.note: according to report means as it is said or heard, so the word for genuine stands for one sounding the same

parts.note: something not fictitious is real

explanation.surface: A claim that part of a film is genuine, not made up, according to reports.
explanation.definitionFit: A spool holding a length of movie, so a feature runs to several of these sections.

clue.text: Exploit amazingly large survey of those who have voted

definitions.text: survey of those who have voted

indicators.note: amazingly suggests something has been startlingly changed, so the letters of exploit are rearranged

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for large, as on clothing

explanation.surface: Someone exploiting a huge survey taken of voters as they leave.
explanation.definitionFit: A poll taken of voters as they leave the polling station, used to forecast the result.

clue.text: Mystic one Spanish painter almost knocked back

indicators.note: knocked back means turned backwards, so one and the shortened painter are read in reverse

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the painter's name loses its last letter

parts.note: Goya was the Spanish painter of the Maja and the Black Paintings

explanation.surface: A mystic and a Spanish painter, nearly knocked over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims GOYA to GOY; 'knocked back' reverses IGOY.
explanation.definitionFit: A Hindu master of meditation practice, regarded as a spiritual sage or mystic.

clue.text: Classification of ox, to many, wrongly applied

indicators.note: wrongly applied suggests putting things in the wrong places, so the letters of ox, to many are reordered

explanation.surface: A complaint that an animal grouping has been mistakenly applied to too many oxen.
explanation.definitionFit: The science of grouping and naming organisms, or any scheme of ordering things into categories.

clue.text: In the end, book is printed on time

parts.note: an atlas is a book of maps

explanation.surface: A book finally being printed on schedule.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is printed on' sets T after the book, as a stamp goes onto the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Said when something comes after a long wait, it is an idiom meaning eventually or finally.

clue.text: Motor yacht went, to pay for film

parts.note: left means went away, departed
to foot the bill is to pay for it

explanation.surface: Someone who sailed off in a motor yacht to pay for a film.
explanation.walkthrough: MY LEFT FOOT is the 1989 film about the Irish writer Christy Brown, starring Daniel Day-Lewis.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the title of a 1989 Irish biographical movie, an example of a film.

clue.text: Not quite willing to study

indicators.note: not quite means falling short, so the last letter of the word for willing is dropped

parts.note: ready means willing, as in ready to help

explanation.surface: A student only half willing to study.
explanation.definitionFit: To pore over books as a student is to study a subject, as in reading law at university.

clue.text: A new member brought over backer

indicators.note: brought over means turned over, so the word for limb is read backwards

parts.note: a leg is a limb, a member of the body

explanation.surface: A new member of a club has been brought over by a backer.
explanation.definitionFit: In theatre an investor who puts money into a show is called by this name, so a financial supporter.

clue.text: Bus son missed left from here, old city in Zimbabwe

indicators.note: missed means lost or left out, so the letter for son drops from bus

parts.note: away means from here, elsewhere

explanation.surface: A traveller's son missed the bus that left from here, an old Zimbabwean city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old' does double duty in the surface; it is O, and 'city in Zimbabwe' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Zimbabwe's second largest city, founded on an old Ndebele royal site, is a city in that country.

clue.text: Commander in Hedda Gabler

indicators.note: in tells us the letters sit inside the play's title, running across the two words

explanation.surface: A military commander appears in Ibsen's play Hedda Gabler.
explanation.definitionFit: An aga is a title for an Ottoman military officer or chief, so a commander.

clue.text: Freaked out after working aloft

indicators.note: after says the word for freaked out goes behind the word for working

parts.note: on means working, as in a machine that is on
high means freaked out, as on drugs

explanation.surface: Someone who went into a panic after a stint working up at a height.
explanation.definitionFit: Up above in the heavens or high in the air is a phrase meaning up above, overhead.

clue.text: Sound level for listeners

indicators.note: for listeners says the word is meant as heard, so the word for level stands for one sounding the same

parts.note: straight means level or even

explanation.surface: A sound engineer setting the volume level for an audience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' looks like noise; it is a narrow channel of sea, as in Plymouth Sound.
explanation.definitionFit: A sound is a narrow stretch of water linking two seas, which is the geographic sense of this word.

clue.text: Pudding poorly cooked, extremely lumpy

indicators.note: cooked means mixed and doctored, so the letters of poorly are reworked
extremely means at the extremes, so the first and last letters of lumpy are taken

explanation.surface: A pudding badly made and very lumpy.
explanation.walkthrough: A ROLY-POLY is a British baked or steamed suet pudding rolled with jam.
explanation.definitionFit: Jam roly-poly is a traditional British suet dessert rolled up with jam, an example of a pudding.
